value.text:
GenUUID only has 7 usages, so that's not a major concern. I should take a broader look at what's exported from the internal packages—maybe there's something in logging utilities or the config/logger setup that's used throughout. Since the server and store packages reference internal functions heavily, I'll write a script to systematically count how many times each internal function is actually called across the repo, excluding its declaration and any test files.

I need to be careful though—interface methods like Validate, Render, Info, and Error might show up multiple times as declarations since they're implemented by different types, and their call counts could be misleading since they're invoked polymorphically through the interface. The real signal I'm looking for is a single utility or helper function with genuinely high inbound call count. Let me automate this by finding all function declarations in internal, then for each unique name, counting how many times that identifier appears followed by an open paren across the entire repo, subtracting out the declarations themselves.

args.command: cd /bench/repo && grep -rhoE '^func\s+(\([^)]*\)\s+)?[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*\(' --include="*.go" internal/ | sed -E 's/^func\s+(\([^)]*\)\s+)?//;s/\($//' | sort -u > /tmp/internal_funcs.txt; wc -l /tmp/internal_funcs.txt
args.description: Extract unique function/method names declared in internal

args.command:
cd /bench/repo && > /tmp/fanin.txt; while read -r fn; do
  esc=$(printf '%s' "$fn" | sed 's/[.[\*^$]/\\&/g')
  total=$(grep -rhoE "[^A-Za-z0-9_.]${esc}\(" --include="*.go" . | wc -l)
  decl=$(grep -rhoE "^func\s+(\([^)]*\)\s+)?${esc}\(" --include="*.go" internal/ | wc -l)
  callsites=$((total - decl))
  echo "$callsites $fn"
done < /tmp/internal_funcs.txt | sort -rn > /tmp/fanin_sorted.txt
head -40 /tmp/fanin_sorted.txt

This unexported helper builds a dialect-specific SQL expression for a JSON-array field. Searching the whole repo (excluding tests, none of which reference it since it's unused there) for call sites of `jsonArrayExpr(` outside its own declaration turns up 16 distinct call expressions, all within `internal/filter/render.go`, e.g.:

```944:954:internal/filter/render.go
func jsonArrayExpr(d DialectName, field Field) string {
	column := qualifyColumn(d, field.Column)
	switch d {
	case DialectSQLite, DialectMySQL:
		return fmt.Sprintf("JSON_EXTRACT(%s, '%s')", column, jsonPath(field))
	case DialectPostgres:
		return buildPostgresJSONAccessor(column, field.JSONPath, false)
	default:
		return ""
	}
}
```

Methodology: I extracted every `func` declaration under `internal/**/*.go`, kept only names with exactly one declaration (to avoid conflating same-named methods on different receivers, e.g. `New`, `Validate`, `Render`), then grepped the whole repo (excluding `_test.go` files) for call-expression occurrences of each name, subtracting the declaration line itself. `jsonArrayExpr` came out on top at 16, ahead of `getConstValue` (13, in `internal/filter`), `Transcribe` (11, in `internal/ai`), and `getIdentName` (7). Two other names, `NewEngine` (32) and `NewSchema` (29), had higher raw counts, but nearly all of those calls were from test files (`engine_test.go`, `functions_test.go`, `time_test.go`); in non-test/production code they're called only twice each, so they don't represent meaningful production fan-in.

Caveat: this is a heuristic, regex-based call-site count (not a true compiler-derived call graph via `go/analysis` or `guru`), so it could miss calls made through function values/interfaces or slightly misattribute in edge cases — but for `jsonArrayExpr` all 16 matches were manually verified as direct, unambiguous calls.
